commit.message: ci(semgrep): actually execute Rule 2's behavioral contract [impact-checked]

intent: Make anti-slop Rule 2's behavioral contract actually execute in CI, and close the five detector gaps decorrelated review found in the rule itself. The tests that prove Rule 2 detects JSONL and SQLite substrates skipped in every automated lane, so a regression removing a detection shape stayed green everywhere - the same defect class as a rule message promising a capability no execution ever checked.

negative_controls.command: python3 -c "import subprocess, sys; from pathlib import Path; p = Path('.semgrep/dharma-anti-slop.yml'); t = p.read_text(); assert '[bt+]*a[bt+]*' in t; p.write_text(t.replace('[bt+]*a[bt+]*', 'a[bt+]*')); r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-m', 'pytest', '-q', 'tests/test_semgrep_rule2_behavior.py'], check=False); p.write_text(t); sys.exit(r.returncode)"
negative_controls.name: reverting-the-append-mode-regex-fails-the-contract

honest_blockers: semgrep is not among main's required status checks (DocOps integrity gate, Coherence Delta PR body, gitleaks, pytest 3.11, pytest 3.12, Onboarding admission parity), so the new rule2-behavior job executes and goes red on a regression but does not block merge until the operator adds it to branch protection. A pull request cannot change branch protection.

Adding semgrep to the dev extra would have put the contract inside the required pytest lanes, but pyproject.toml is an owned surface of the dharmagraph-engine-2026-07 track, so that route trespasses on sibling ownership. The workflow route was chosen for that reason as well as dependency isolation.
The 17 strict-scan findings remain OWNER_DEFERRED and unadjudicated; this work changed none of them, and the count and file:line set are unchanged.
Two named detector gaps cannot be expressed as fixture lines: the class-name boundary is a deliberate negative control, and the same-canonical-file collision is path-scoped.
interface_mismatches: tests/conftest.py carries an autouse fixture that imports dharma_swarm.agent_runner, so a scanner-only CI lane must run the behavioral file with --noconftest; the test module itself imports nothing from the package.
open_broken_register_items: The behavioral contract for Rule 2 skipped in every automated lane: the pytest jobs install .[dev], which declares no scanner, and the semgrep container ran only production scans.

Rule 2's append detector required a leading 'a' in the mode literal, missed qualified path-first opens such as aiofiles.open(path, 'a'), matched an exempt base only in leading position, and gated exempt-name collisions on 'declares exactly one base'.
session_entry.rollback: Revert the seven-commit range on this branch. Rule 2 returns to its 2026-08-04 detector scope and the behavioral tests return to skipping in every automated lane; no runtime, no daemon and no merge authority is affected.
